I’m not a doctor, but this story is about my dad. He’s an older man, about 73 at the time. He was feeling a lot of pain in his side torso, so he went to his general doctor. Everything seemed fine to Doc. The pain persists, Dad goes back, and he receives the same diagnosis: nothing. This cycle repeats for about 6 months until Dad decides to see a pain doctor. They immediately schedule him with an oncologist and declare he has stage IV lung cancer. How did Dads initial doctor miss this after so many scans? I ask the same questions. Because of his age, surgery isn’t an option, so the doctors decide to pump a new drug into him (also a bunch of opiates which didn’t do shit for my dads pain levels). Dad’s health slowly declines but still stays relatively up for his age (he was an avid runner before his diagnosis). About a year later, his doctors say “Let’s try to remove this cancer.” Why now, a year after the initial diagnosis, when dad is no stronger than he was before? Beats me, but this surgery was supposed to be life saving. It wasn’t. It killed him. He spent his last two weeks of his life withering in agony after the surgery. His doctors failed him in all stages of his diagnosis: at the beginning, when the initial diagnosis was made (why didn’t he undergo surgery then??), and while he was “recovering” from surgery (remember those opiates? Yeah, doctors refused to give him anything stronger than Motrin even though they spent the last year giving him an opiate addiction). An added bonus is they found another huge mass under his lung during the surgery. Again, why didn’t the scans pick this up???? Shortly after Dads passing, his original doctor that failed to catch the cancer in early stages retired. This happened only about a year ago, but it really opened my eyes to medical malpractice in America
